blogs.title: FlashAttention Then & Now: How GPUs Are Finally Unblocking Transformer Attention
blogs.description: Trace the evolution of FlashAttention from its original version through FlashAttention‑2 to the newest breakthrough FlashAttention‑3. Explain why attention remains the computational bottleneck in large language models and long‑context tasks, highlight the limitations encountered on NVIDIA’s Hopper H100 GPUs, and show how Stripe’s new warps specialization and low‑precision tricks bring real speedups.

blogs.title: Warp‑Specialization Made Simple – Boosting GPU Performance with Producer/Consumer Warps
blogs.description: Demystify the technique of partitioning a warpgroup into producer (data‑loading) and consumer (compute) warps. Use analogies such as an assembly line to illustrate how asynchronous Tensor Memory Accelerators (TMA) and WGMMA GEMMs can run in parallel, leading to a measurable 1½–2× acceleration on modern GPUs.

blogs.title: FP8 At Scale – Why Low‑Precision Significantly Speeds Attention Without Losing Accuracy
blogs.description: Unpack how Hopper’s new FP8 Tensor Cores double throughput over FP16 while keeping accuracy intact. Delve into block‑wise quantization and incoherent processing that tame outliers in language models, resulting in a whopping 2.6× reduction in numerical error compared with naïve per‑tensor quantization.

blogs.title: "Ping‑Pong" Scheduling — The Art of Overlapping Softmax with Matrix Multiplications
blogs.description: Explain the concept of interleaving softmax calculations with successive GEMM stages inside a single warpgroup. Show how trickily arranged barriers let special function units work concurrently with Tensor Cores, shaving milliseconds off every inference step.

blogs.title: [Benchmark] FlashAttention‑3 vs. Industry Standards—What It Means for Real‑World LLMs
blogs.description: Present side‑by‑side numbers comparing FlashAttention‑3 against standard PyTorch attention, older FlashAttention variants, and cuDNN’s optimised kernels on an H100 GPU. Highlight peak performance figures (up to 740 TFLOPs/s for FP16 and near 1 PFLOPs/s for FP8) and explain what these gains translate into for training long documents or multimodal content.
